counter {

        public:
            run() -> bool {
                value >> int <- 0;
                while (value < 3) {
                    value <- value + 1;
                }

            }

    ref main ->> run;

    fa:
        return true;
}

Places and functions

A typed place, an explicit write, a named function and a declared entry point.

About this example

The example returns a bool. The entry point is selected by ref main; the function name alone has no entry-point privilege.

View original sourceRead the contract
[@]Reference fixture
rootCore[@] {
    stc:
        rootAddr: addr;
        rootWord: word;

    binary:
        @rootWord >> word : 0b1;

    bind:
        @rootAddr >> addr : 0b1;

    raw {
    }

    fn:
        rootCheck() -> bool {
            public:
                return true;
        }

    fa:
        return true;
}

Foundational contracts

Root declarations express the foundations that other language levels depend on.

About this example

This is a source-inspection fixture. Read its contract alongside the compiler route and target profile.

View original sourceRead the contract
[@machine]Explicit overflow branch
machineCheckedAdd[@machine] {
    reg:
        rax;
        rbx;

    label:
        entryPoint;
        overflow;
        finish;

    inst:
        entryPoint:
        add rax, rbx;
        jmp.ov overflow;
        jmp finish;

        overflow:
        halt;

        finish:
        ret;

    final:
        ret;
}

Typed machine control flow

Registers, labels, instructions and the final remain visible in the source model.

About this example

jmp.ov follows the add result into an explicit overflow path. This does not enable automatic checked arithmetic for every operation.

View original sourceRead the contract
primitive[@]Inspection fixture
primitive[@]:
    capability material_io:
        allow port.read;
        allow port.write;

    port uart0.data:
        addr ioaddr(0x03F8);

    port uart0.status:
        addr ioaddr(0x03FD);

    operation kernelEntry():
        capability material_io;
        portWrite uart0.data <- 0x41;
        portRead uart0.status;
        mmioWrite 0x0040 <- 0x01 volatile;
        mmioRead 0x0040 volatile;
        read side_effect none;
        volatileWrite 0x0050 <- 0x02;
        volatileRead 0x0050;
        fence;
        cpuPause;
        haltLoop;

    anchor:
        boot0;

    bridge:
        root.memory.resolve;

    seal:
        primitiveClosed;

Material operations

Capabilities and material operations describe the contract at the hardware boundary.

About this example

This fixture includes privileged operations. It is for source inspection; execution requires the appropriate profile, permissions and hardware.

For systems programmers

More of the contract
belongs in the language.

The goal is C-class control with a wider, continuous model. These are the design choices behind that goal.

[@machine]

A typed machine boundary

GNU extended asm describes instructions through a template and operand constraints. nC's machine layer represents instructions, labels and control transfers in the language model, with contracts carried through semantic analysis and IR.

Read the machine-layer contractC context: GCC extended asm
size / align / ABI

Representation you can inspect

Layout, alignment and calling conventions change what a program does. nC treats representation and linkage as part of its continuous model. Memory remains manual/raw: allocation, valid addresses and release stay under program control.

Read about memory and representation
source → IR → image

A compiler you can trace

The path from a declaration to native bytes should be inspectable. ncc exposes analysis and emission routes; the public bootstrap records source identities, providers and artifact comparisons for named generations.

Inspect the compiler phasesReview the published evidence

nC is in active native bootstrap. The public edition's documented contracts define today's supported scope; they are the starting point for evaluating the language.

The idea behind nC

One language.
Every layer.

A function, a pointer, an instruction and a linked image belong to the same program. nC is being built to keep their contracts connected.
